types.embedding_query_text: Musician: A person who composes, conducts, or performs music. Also called Artist, Performer, Composer, Singer. Examples: Harry Styles, Niall, Louis, Zayn.

chosen_type.label: MusicGroup
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org MusicGroup definition explicitly includes 'solo musician', which fits all the mentions.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: SheetMusic
candidates.comment: Printed or written musical notation, as distinct from a performance or recording. Also called musical score, notation, music manuscript, song sheet. Examples: a piano concerto score, guitar tablature, a vocal sheet for a song, an orchestral score.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or honor bestowed for achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Accolade, Recognition. Examples: Guinness World Record, Brit Awards, Grammy Awards, Ivor Novello Awards.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A prize or honor bestowed for achievement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an 'Award' as an entity; existing candidates are events or actions. 'Thing' is the most appropriate general parent.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: WinAction

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31. Also called Calendar year, Annual period, Twelvemonth. Examples: 2025, 2010, 2016, 2024.

chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class specifically represents a 'Year' as a conceptual entity; 'Date' is a datatype, and other candidates are irrelevant. 'Intangible' is the closest parent for a conceptual time period.

candidates.label: Schedule

Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Will Munford, Anne Twist, Gemma, Guinness World Records adjudicator Will Munford.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person class is an exact match for the OIE type and definition.

candidates.label: Person

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician

Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: GenderType
candidates.comment: A GenderType is an Enumeration of genders. Also called sex, gender identity. Examples: Male, Female, NonBinary.

chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class specifically represents a 'MusicTour'. 'Trip' is the most appropriate parent as a tour is a type of journey.

types.embedding_query_text: SocialMediaPlatform: An online service that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking. Also called Social network, Online platform, Social site. Examples: X.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform

Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration

Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: Brazil, Mexico, US, Australia.

candidates.label: Country

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater

Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: CityHall

Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Zoo
